name: Relay settings change (the four-step procedure)
description: The owner's four steps, 2026-09-15, as one authored procedure — the legacy program's A/M/P procedure as it worked: (1) an engineer raises the change against a protective relay and says why; (2) the engineer completes the rationale documentation and the settings file — two tracks, side by side; (3) when both are complete the request progresses to the field (the join, then the outage window); (4) field staff install and commission the settings, after which the work request is completed and the new revision is the in-service one — the legacy M becoming the A and the A becoming the P. The legacy's third check box (the relay software) is not a step: the platform's own record of the file is that check. Authored to prove #165: no code was written for this procedure or its screens.

items.title: [1] Request the change and say why
items.instruction: Say what the change is for and which relay or relays it covers. Committing this step creates the settings-issue package the rest of the work fills.

items.title: [2] Rationale and settings — both before the field

body.title: Rationale document
body.instruction: Attach the rationale for the change: what is being changed, why, and what was considered.

body.title: Settings for every relay in the change
A settings file for a microprocessor relay; a text file for anything else
Settings file from the vendor tool
body.instruction: Attach the settings file for this relay. It becomes the outstanding revision in the settings book (the legacy M).

else.title: Settings as a text file
else.instruction: No vendor file exists for this relay: attach the settings as a text file in name=value form. It becomes the outstanding revision in the settings book (the legacy M).

items.title: [3] To the field — wait for the outage window, if one is required

body.title: Settings installed and commissioned
body.instruction: Load the settings to the relay and commission them. Record when. Captured in the field and checked in, or committed here.

items.title: Work request completed — the new settings are the in-service settings
items.instruction: The settings book now says this is the truth: the new revision goes in service and the one it replaces is archived (the M becomes the A, the A becomes the P).
